notes: Read all 67 source lines with line numbers before porting. Imports (L1-5): useEffect/useState (L1) kept (plus useRef added for the Animated width); react-i18next useTranslation (L2) replaced by an inline English-default t(key, fallback); cn() (L3) dropped — Tailwind class composition becomes a React Native StyleSheet; useMotionPreference (L4) replaced by an inline native useMotionPreference backed by AccessibilityInfo.isReduceMotionEnabled() + the 'reduceMotionChanged' event, returning the same { reduce, durationMs } shape; globalProgress (L5) inlined as a byte-for-byte faithful port of @/lib/globalProgress (pure Set+setInterval+Math, no DOM) and re-exported so future consumers share the singleton + start/stop concurrency contract.

Doc comment (L7-29) preserved and adapted into the component JSDoc + header banner: the slim 2px top strip, the subscribe-to-globalProgress activation, the disappear-on-zero behavior, the gradient/glow visual, the asymptotic-trickle width, the progressbar a11y semantics, and the prefers-reduced-motion honoring (bar still shown, transition omitted) are all carried over. The cyan->indigo->emerald gradient note is annotated with the native collapse to the solid cyan accent token because React Native has no CSS gradient and no gradient library is installed.

Component signature export function TopProgress() (L30) preserved (zero-arg callable via `= {}` default) plus optional native composition props (style/testID) — style documents that RN position:'absolute' is ancestor-relative, so the host renders <TopProgress /> inside its full-screen root as the analog of the DOM viewport-fixed layer. useTranslation() (L31) -> inline t. useMotionPreference() destructure of { reduce } (L32) preserved against the inline native hook. useState(false) active (L34) and useState(0) progress (L35) preserved (the progress state is named progressValue to free the module-level `progress` trickle accumulator inside the inlined controller; the state semantics are identical).

Subscribe effect (L37-42): the useEffect returning globalProgress.subscribe((nextActive, nextProgress) => { setActive; setProgress }) is ported verbatim with the identical empty [] deps and the same teardown-via-returned-unsubscribe contract. Early return if (!active) return null (L44) preserved exactly, and kept after every hook (useMotionPreference's internal hooks, the two useState, the subscribe useEffect, the useRef width value, and the width-animation useEffect all run unconditionally before it) so React hook order is stable.

valuenow computation (L46) Math.round(Math.max(0, Math.min(100, progress))) ported verbatim; it is hoisted above the early return (a pure computation, behavior-identical) so the width-animation effect can depend on it while preserving unconditional hook order. Render (L48-66): outer <div role='progressbar' aria-label aria-valuemin/valuemax/valuenow data-testid> -> <Animated.View accessibilityRole='progressbar' accessibilityLabel={t('global.loading','Loading')} accessibilityValue={{min:0,max:100,now:valuenow}} testID='top-progress'>. aria-valuemin=0 (L52) -> min:0; aria-valuemax=100 (L53) -> max:100; aria-valuenow=valuenow (L54) -> now:valuenow.

className positioning (L57) fixed top-0 left-0 right-0 z-[60] h-0.5 pointer-events-none -> styles.bar position:'absolute' top/left/right:0 zIndex:60 height:2 (h-0.5 = 2px) + pointerEvents='none'. Gradient (L58) bg-gradient-to-r from-cyan-400 via-indigo-400 to-emerald-400 -> backgroundColor colors.accent (#35d5ff cyan, the gradient's leading/dominant tone) — documented as a native-safe collapse of the multi-stop gradient since RN ships no gradient primitive. Glow (L59) shadow-[0_0_8px_rgba(34,211,238,0.55)] -> shadowColor '#22d3ee' shadowOpacity 0.55 shadowRadius 8 shadowOffset {0,0} + elevation 4 (Android), the faithful analog of the cyan glow.

Reduced-motion + width (L60-64): the web `reduce ? null : 'transition-[width] duration-fast ease-linear'` branch (L60-62) and style={{ width: `${valuenow}%` }} (L64) become an Animated.Value interpolated to a percentage string ['0%','100%']; when reduce is true the width is set instantly via widthAnim.setValue(valuenow) (no smoothing — exactly the null/omitted-transition branch), and when motion is allowed it eases linearly (Easing.linear) over DURATION_FAST_MS=150 (the resolved --motion-duration-fast token) with useNativeDriver:false because width is a layout prop. Closing tags L65-67 and the trailing newline (L68) accounted for.

Behavior, state names (active/progress), the globalProgress subscribe API and trickle contract (TRICKLE_TARGET=80, TRICKLE_INITIAL=8, TRICKLE_INTERVAL_MS=120), the valuenow 0..100 clamp, the i18n key (global.loading -> 'Loading'), and the progressbar a11y semantics are all preserved. No API paths or unit-suffixed fields are involved. No DOM-only modules, browser HTML elements, Recharts, Leaflet, or old web UI components are imported; the only browser-only dependency (the gradient + viewport-fixed layer) is replaced with documented native-safe equivalents.
